speaker: Warren Ashford
cascadeSummary: District 7 demands verifiable fiscal performance before authorizing new appropriations and establishes strict post-occupancy audit benchmarks for Temescal and KONO. While upbeat sentiment in Rockridge, Temescal, and KONO reflects local merchant resilience, slow street trade in Temescal proves that ribbon-cuttings do not replace sustained municipal service delivery and commercial corridor support. I am demanding hard audit metrics for the Downtown Economic Revitalization fund ahead of the Cycle 112 committee hearing and ensuring every public dollar spent in District 7 is fully accounted for.

statements.topic: District 7 Commercial Corridors and Service Delivery
statements.decision: Mandate municipal service auditing for KONO and targeted commercial revitalization tracking for Temescal merchant corridors.
statements.quote: Temescal's resilience and KONO's stability are built on merchant discipline and strict oversight, not mayoral victory laps.
statements.fullStatement: Low crime and upbeat sentiment across Rockridge, KONO, and Temescal demonstrate the resilience of District 7's business districts and residents. However, slow street trade in Temescal shows we cannot afford complacency or symbolic gestures. Credit belongs to the local shopkeepers and neighborhood associations managing tight margins, and City Hall must answer by delivering audited, dependable municipal maintenance and safety services along Telegraph and Broadway. District 7 will continue tracking public service delivery metrics to guarantee our small businesses receive the basic city support their tax dollars fund.

statements.topic: Temescal Community Health Center Utilization Audit
statements.decision: Enforce post-occupancy clinical intake audits and line-item expenditure reconciliations on remaining facility allocations.
statements.quote: Operational status is merely a baseline—District 7 will audit every intake metric and every remaining dollar of this allocation.
statements.fullStatement: With the Temescal Community Health Center operational, our focus pivots strictly from construction sign-offs to post-occupancy performance audits. District 7 requires quarterly utilization reviews tracking patient intake efficiency and service delivery across Temescal, Rockridge, and KONO. We must verify that the remaining capital balance produces measurable healthcare outcomes rather than administrative overhead. A successful capital project must demonstrate clinical throughput and rigorous cost accounting on the city ledger.

statements.decision: Condition consideration of downtown revitalization funds on performance-indexed audit standards and line-item transparency at the Cycle 112 committee hearing.
statements.quote: A multi-million-dollar downtown fund must come with line-item benchmarks and verified return on investment before a single check clears.
statements.fullStatement: As the Mayor calls an emergency Economic Development Committee hearing for Cycle 112, I reiterate my demand for transparent, performance-indexed criteria on the Downtown Economic Revitalization proposal. Revitalizing commercial districts requires verifiable return-on-investment metrics, not discretionary slush funds. I will enter that hearing demanding clear disbursement milestones, clawback provisions for unspent capital, and strict auditing mechanisms before any downtown appropriation receives my vote.
